text:
The recent turnover in safety leadership at OpenAI is a stark reminder that managing AI isn’t just about technology — it’s fundamentally about people and processes. 

1️⃣ **Understanding Complexity**: When I first dived into product management, I believed that having the right tech was the key to success. Now, I see that the people navigating this tech are equally crucial. OpenAI’s leadership challenges underscore that if your team isn’t aligned and equipped to handle the unpredictability of AI, even the best models can falter.

2️⃣ **Collaborative Decision-Making**: In my previous roles, I learned the hard way that hoarding decisions stifles innovation. The rapid changes at OpenAI illustrate the need for diverse voices in leadership — the more perspectives we bring into discussions about AI ethics and safety, the better our products will reflect user needs and societal values.

3️⃣ **Guardrails Matter**: The recent shifts remind me of a time when I misjudged the importance of data governance. I prioritized speed over accuracy, leading to downstream issues. With AI, ensuring robust guardrails is non-negotiable.

Let’s not just manage AI; let’s lead with intention and clarity, especially when the stakes are so high.
